could we make sure that goldens only runs under development env flag or if that is an anti patern to the repo path develop . and maybe a flag on that whole thing

Checked toolpath wip/bdelanghe (151e379). There are two separate pieces, and they want different answers.

1. The `path goldens` subcommand ships in the release binary today. It is only gated off for emscripten (crates/path-cli/src/lib.rs:141), and release.yml builds `-p path-cli --bin path` with default features. That should get a flag. The repo already has the pattern: `resume-remote` is a Cargo feature, off by default, that hides experimental commands and their deps. Proposal: a `goldens` feature on path-cli, off by default, gating `mod goldens` and the `Goldens` subcommand. The release stays as is, and dev builds use `cargo run --features goldens -- goldens check`.

2. `cargo test -p toolpath-goldens` (the snippet you commented on): I would NOT put this behind an env flag. The crate is already `publish = false`, so it never ships. An env-var skip turns the per-PR gate (decided 10-16: gate stays on every PR) into a silent pass whenever the variable is missing. That is the same failure mode as the qualifier silent pass we flagged on the wip. If "develop" means the nix devShell, the devShell and CI can set it explicitly instead, e.g. `--features goldens` in the check. A test that skips quietly is the anti-pattern.

show this is there a test framework we built. and this shows up in the request right?

Yes to both. The framework is ours: the toolpath-webmock crate. It is one local server that records an agent's real API traffic once and then replays it with no upstream and fake credentials, and each agent is pointed at it with its own base-URL switch (this slide). And yes, the projected session is in the request: the saved codex → claude recording's POST /v1/messages carries the projected conversation as 5 messages (user/assistant alternating, starting with codex's permissions text and its wc -w turn). So a replayed resume proves the history actually reached the model's request, not just the screen.
can we dig into the copilot issue

Dug in. Root cause is in our replay keying, not in copilot or GitHub.

Copilot makes three POSTs to GitHub's remote MCP server at /mcp/readonly: initialize (id 0), notifications/initialized, tools/list (id 1). On replay the JSON-RPC ids and progress tokens differ, so the exact key misses. The fallback "loose" key is {method, path, model, last user text}, and an MCP request has neither a model nor user text, so all three POSTs share one loose key. The first stored cassette wins, and tools/list gets the wrong answer. Copilot then sees 0 MCP tools instead of 6, so its model request carries 19 tools instead of 25 ($.tools.19-24 only in the recording), and every /v1/messages call misses (rc 1 after 5 retries, 151 s).

Fix: when a body is JSON-RPC, put its method in the loose key, and drop id and params._meta.progressToken when normalizing. Then tools/list replays tools/list, the tool list stays 25, and the model request should key EXACT. Dispatching that now as its own piece (pr/21) on toolpath wip: a unit test for the collision, then a re-run of the copilot replay cell (no network, fake credentials) to show EXACT before claiming it.
what does this page mean should/could we use truffle hog.

What it means: this one is staged too, like the break slide. Cassettes are recorded API exchanges we commit, so a real credential could end up in git (it nearly did: the first gemini recording wrote your real key). The no_secrets test scans every committed fixture with the rules in .gitleaks.toml, and the same file drives the gitleaks gate in CI and home's pre-commit hook (#416). The demo plants a fake sk-ant key, the test fails naming file:line and the rule, then it is reverted. v12 says that on the slide.

TruffleHog: yes as an addition, not a replacement. gitleaks stays the gate, because it is offline, deterministic, and its one rules file is shared by cargo test, CI and the hook. TruffleHog (3.97.9 in nixpkgs) adds many more detectors and can verify a hit by calling the provider. Verification means sending the found secret over the network, so it does not belong in cargo test or CI on fixtures. Where it fits: home's pre-push hook, running trufflehog git file://. --since-commit <upstream> --results=verified,unknown --fail, so a live key is caught before it leaves the machine; plus a one-off full-history scan of toolpath and pathbase. Want me to add that to the home hook as its own PR?

comments.body: can we fix all of these defects

Yes. Dispatching three agents, grouped by the code each fix touches. Each fix lands as its own piece on toolpath wip with its own pr/NN record, and each one deletes its known_defects entry in the same commit, so the check proves it is gone:
1. Claude writer (two defects): codex → claude stops writing event types Claude never emits (agent_message, token_count, …) and maps them to Claude's own; claude → claude writes stop_reason, not stopReason.
2. Codex writer: claude → codex keeps the source session's working directory instead of writing /. If that turns out to be an artifact of the hermetic test setup rather than a real bug, it says so instead of changing code.
3. Token accounting (three defects): gemini and opencode keep reasoning-token breakdowns in the document totals (489 and 285 today), and copilot puts its session totals on the steps.
Every piece runs the full gates before it is pushed. I will post here when they land.
can we look at all the gains those are most concerning

Agreed, they are worse than the losses. I went through every gained key across all 54 round-trip snapshots (most: 39 new fields, gemini through codex), and they sort into three kinds. v19 adds them as slide 5.
1. Invented values that look real: a Claude session written for Codex claims model_provider "openai", cli_version "0.0.0-projected", originator "codex-toolpath"; every session written for Claude gets permissionMode "default"; opencode and pi get a stop_reason; Claude, Gemini and pi grow sub-agent delegations (id, prompt, result) that were never there.
2. File changes that never happened: opencode turns a failed read of does-not-exist.txt into a file change, and edits come back filed under absolute temp paths (/private/var/folders/…) instead of notes.md.
3. Translation, not invention: tool inputs renamed into each agent's own words, the working directory, the writer's producer stamp.
The check only counts gained keys, not their values, which is why 1 and 2 pass today. Once the six-defect fixes land (they touch the same writers), I will dispatch fixes for 1 and 2 and make the check compare values of fields the source never had.
we are fixing these issues? what is the mechanism that causes each? lets start with read.

Yes, we are fixing them. Read column, mechanism by mechanism (gemini and cursor read are fixed and shown ok):

pi, "lossy · provider": pi records the provider on every message ("provider": "ollama", "model": "gemma4") and in model_change entries. The document has no field for a provider: a turn carries the model name only. So the pi reader keeps the provider only in its pi-private extras (Turn.extra.pi), and it drops model_change entries outright (there is a test named test_model_change_drops_silently). Any other agent's writer never sees the provider. Written back to pi without those extras, pi's writer falls back to its default, "anthropic", so ollama/gemma4 comes back as anthropic/gemma4 (qualifier f898c8ff). The fix belongs in the shared document: give a turn a provider, set it in every reader that knows it, and use it in every writer. That touches toolpath-convo, the crate every agent shares, so it is a design call Alex should see. I would add an optional provider on the turn, not overload the model string.

opencode, "defect · tokens": opencode records reasoning tokens per message (breakdowns.output.reasoning, 285 in the golden). The reader puts them on each step, but the session total in the document is rebuilt from four counters only (input, output, cache read, cache write), so the reasoning breakdown never reaches the total, and the per-step sums and the total disagree. Gemini had the same shape (489). Both are in the accounting fix already running.

Next I will do the write column the same way. Want the provider fix dispatched now, or written up for Alex first?

does toolpath already have a key for extended values a clean place for gains. rather than polluting the namespace. does the code explicitly call out these gains in the harness transformers?

Short answer: yes, there is a clean place, but the gains do not use it, and the code names them only in comments.

Where extended values already live:
- In the conversation view (IR), every turn has extra, keyed by harness: Turn.extra["claude"], ["pi"], ["gemini"]. The codex writer's own docs say foreign namespaces are dropped "so they would not pollute the JSONL".
- In the document, the agent-coding-session kind allows extra properties, and each harness's native leftovers ride in the conversation.append structural change (entry_extra), next to the shared fields.

Why gains pollute anyway: a writer fills in values the target harness needs, the target's reader reads them back as if the harness had written them, and they land as ordinary fields in that harness's namespace. Nothing marks them as made up.

Do the transformers call them out? Only in comments, not in the data:
- codex/project.rs module docs: "For non-Codex sources, the projector synthesizes sensible defaults (originator "codex-toolpath", source "cli", model_provider "openai")", plus cli_version "0.0.0-projected" at line 233. originator is deliberately a marker ("so Codex-side tooling can tell projected sessions from real ones"), and nothing reads that marker back.
- claude/project.rs:81: "emit a default permission-mode line so Claude Code can resume them" ("permissionMode": "default").
- path-cli/projection/codex.rs:102-105: "openai" when the source has no provider.

Proposal:
(1) Every writer records what it synthesized in one place, a toolpath namespace (e.g. extra.toolpath.synthesized: the key paths it filled and why) or a recognisable marker, as codex already does with originator.
(2) Readers that see toolpath's own marker keep those values out of the shared fields, or flag them.
(3) The goldens split gains into "synthesized, declared by the writer" and "undeclared". Only undeclared gains fail, and the check compares values, not just keys.
This also fixes the invented-values row on slide 5 at the root. Want it dispatched after the current fixes land? It touches the same writers.

It also has tests for each harness's setup that do not need the agent binaries, and it is verified in replay against the committed recordings. I will update this slide when it lands.
